label: Symplectic Fibrations
notes: This chapter, printed pages 252 through 288, builds the theory of bundles whose fibers are symplectic manifolds. The recurring move is to split a total space into base motion and fiber geometry, then ask when fiberwise symplectic data assembles into a global closed form whose holonomy records Hamiltonian information about the structure group.

label: Symplectic Fibrations Defined
notes: A symplectic fibration is a locally trivial bundle whose fibers carry symplectic forms varying smoothly and whose transition maps act by symplectomorphisms. The fiberwise form is intrinsic to each fiber but is not yet a form on the total space, so the central problem is extension across horizontal directions.

label: Two-Sphere Bundles
notes: Oriented two-sphere bundles are the smallest interesting symplectic fibrations because every area form on the two-sphere is symplectic. They illustrate how the topology of the base, captured by an Euler class or a clutching map, controls whether the fiberwise area forms can be glued into a coherent global symplectic structure.

label: The Symplectic Connection
notes: Given a fiberwise symplectic form, the horizontal distribution is the symplectic orthogonal complement of the vertical tangent space. This complement is a genuine connection because the fiberwise form is nondegenerate on the fibers, so horizontal and vertical subspaces meet transversally and span the whole tangent space of the total space.

label: Horizontal Lifts
notes: A base path lifts uniquely to horizontal curves once a starting fiber point is fixed. Parallel transport along that path carries one fiber to another, and because the horizontal distribution is the symplectic orthogonal, this transport is a symplectomorphism between the fibers, preserving the fiberwise areas it moves.

label: Curvature
notes: Curvature measures the failure of horizontal lifts to close: the bracket of two horizontal lifts has a vertical component. For the symplectic connection this vertical component is a Hamiltonian vector field on the fiber, so curvature is valued in Hamiltonian functions rather than arbitrary fiber vector fields.

label: Holonomy
notes: Transport around a closed base loop returns to the starting fiber but generally rotates it by a nontrivial symplectomorphism, the holonomy. The notebook model computes a holonomy angle equal to integrated curvature times enclosed base area, the local prototype of how curvature accumulates into global fiber automorphisms.

label: The Coupling Form
notes: The coupling form is the distinguished closed extension of the fiberwise symplectic form, normalized so its integral over each fiber is fixed and its horizontal part is tied to the connection. It combines a vertical fiber contribution with a base contribution built from the curvature Hamiltonians of the connection.

label: Closed Extension Condition
notes: A fiberwise symplectic form extends to a closed two-form on the total space exactly when the curvature Hamiltonians can be chosen consistently, an obstruction living in fiberwise cohomology. When the fibers have vanishing first cohomology the obstruction disappears and a canonical closed coupling form always exists.

label: Hamiltonian Fibrations
notes: A Hamiltonian fibration is a symplectic fibration whose structure group reduces to the group of Hamiltonian symplectomorphisms. Equivalently the fiberwise form extends to a closed form whose fiber integral is fixed, so the holonomy and curvature both take values in Hamiltonian data rather than merely symplectic data.

label: Coupling on Hamiltonian Fibration
notes: On a Hamiltonian fibration the coupling form is canonical and closed, and its top fiber power computes characteristic numbers of the bundle. Choosing it amounts to choosing a connection whose holonomy lies in the Hamiltonian group, linking the geometry of the bundle to the topology of that group.

label: Topology of Ham
notes: These constructions feed back into the study of the Hamiltonian group itself. Loops in Ham build Hamiltonian fibrations over the two-sphere, and the coupling form detects nontrivial classes, so symplectic fibrations become a tool for proving that Ham has rich homotopy and cohomology.

label: Summary
notes: We saw fibers plus a connection whose horizontal distribution is the symplectic orthogonal, holonomy acting by symplectomorphisms, and a coupling form packaging fiber and base contributions. Hamiltonian fibrations sharpen this picture and connect it to the topology of Ham, setting up the global rigidity results that follow.
